newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo railways need state help to recover - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo railways need state help to recover - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia's rail company Zeleznicko Transportno Preduzece (ZTP) is ready to engage local metal and electrical equipment firms to upgrade capacities, but needs state help to do so, daily Politika said on Thursday.

"We want to engage local industries in revitalisation, modernisation and construction of new capacities," ZTP official David Vojinovic was quoted by the Belgrade daily as telling a meeting of railroad and industry officials on Wednesday.
Vojinovic said it was very important for domestic firms to establish technological links with foreign partners for renewal of railroad capacities.
"A plan has already been drawn up to rehabilitate diesel engines on which the General Motors company would be engaged along with Yugoslav firms," he said.
According to Vojinovic, the railroad was now operating at 40 percent capacity, with daily volume of freight down to around seven million tonnes, far below the pre-sanctions level.
Out of a total of 9,000 cargo wagons, only 2,500 are in full working order.
"Both wagons and engines are repaired by taking parts off one to build into another," Vojinovic said.
Serbian Chamber of Commerce vice president Momir Pavlicevic said ZTP was in the worst position among public enterprises and that without help from the state there could be no recovery.
"The condition of the rolling stock and rail infrastucture is alarming," said ZTP Srbija official Milovan Krivokapic.
Around 40,000 people are employed by the railroad and 60,000 more by related industries.
Yugoslav metal complex firms said the main obstacle to cooperation with ZTP was the railroad's inability to finance programmes and repay old debts.

Electrical equipment firm Elektronska Industrija Nis general manager Vojislav Mitic urged the Serbian government to find an urgent solution for ZTP's problems, including the sector's privatisation with both local and foreign capital. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
